# Server Signatures (Sentinel)

The library supports server signatures and integration with ALTCHA Sentinel. To process verifications generated by Sentinel, configure the HMAC secret using the API key’s secret value. The verification result will include `verificationData` returned by Sentinel.

```ts
const HMAC_SECRET = 'sec_...'; // Use the API key's secret value

const altcha = create({
  // ...

  hmacSignatureSecret: HMAC_SECRET,
});
```

## Notes

* Do not use the `/challenge` endpoint. Challenges are generated by the Sentinel server.
* Your server only verifies ALTCHA payloads created by Sentinel.

For more details about the differences between self-contained and Sentinel verification, see the documentation:
[https://altcha.org/docs/v2/server-verification/](https://altcha.org/docs/v2/server-verification/)

## Verification data checks

`verifyServerSignature` (and the framework plugins, which call it) checks the signature, `verified` and `expire` from the signed `verificationData`:

* The payload is expired as soon as the current time passes `expire` (Unix seconds), with the same comparison `verifySolution` uses.
* If `expire` is missing or empty, the payload does not expire. Sentinel leaves `expire` empty when the challenge itself has no `expiresAt`. Configure a store to prevent replays of such payloads (see [`/docs/store.md`](/docs/store.md)).
* A payload without a string `signature` returns `invalidSignature: true`.

### Form fields hash

When the widget sends form fields to Sentinel for classification, Sentinel adds `fields` (field names) and `fieldsHash` (SHA-256 of their values) to `verificationData`. Neither `verifyServerSignature` nor the framework plugins compare them with the submitted form. Call `verifyFieldsHash` yourself to reject submissions whose fields were changed after classification:

```ts
import { verifyFieldsHash } from 'altcha-lib';

app.post('/submit', altcha.middleware(), async (req, res) => {
  const verification = res.locals.altcha?.verification;
  const data =
    verification && 'verificationData' in verification
      ? verification.verificationData
      : null;
  if (data?.fields && data.fieldsHash) {
    const valid = await verifyFieldsHash({
      formData: req.body,
      fields: data.fields,
      fieldsHash: data.fieldsHash,
    });
    if (!valid) {
      return res.status(403).json({ error: 'Form fields were modified.' });
    }
  }
  // ...
});
```

## Remote verification (Sentinel API)

Instead of verifying the HMAC signature locally, you can call Sentinel's `/v1/verify/signature` API directly with `verifyServer`. This avoids managing the HMAC secret in your server, at the cost of a network round-trip:

```ts
import { verifyServer } from 'altcha-lib';

const result = await verifyServer({
  payload, // the payload received from POST /v1/verify
  url: 'https://sentinel.example.com/v1/verify/signature',
  secret: API_KEY_SECRET, // optional, checked against the payload's API key
  timeout: 10_000,
  retries: 2,
});

if (result.verified) {
  // ...
}
```

### Using remote verification with framework plugins

All framework plugins (Express, Fastify, NestJS, Next.js, Nuxt/H3, SvelteKit, Hono) accept
a `verifyServer` option. When set, payloads submitted through `middleware` (or SvelteKit's
`createHandle`/`verifyEvent`) are verified remotely via `verifyServer` instead of locally, so
you don't need to configure `hmacSignatureSecret` at all:

```ts
const altcha = create({
  verifyServer: {
    url: 'https://sentinel.example.com/v1/verify/signature',
    secret: API_KEY_SECRET, // optional
    timeout: 10_000,
    retries: 2,
  },
});
```

`deriveKey` and `createChallengeParameters` are also optional — they're only needed for
`challengeHandler` and for verifying self-hosted (non-Sentinel) payloads. If you're relying
entirely on Sentinel to issue and sign challenges, omit all three and don't wire up
`challengeHandler`.

**Note:** `verifyHandler` (the standalone `/verify` endpoint intended for custom, external
integrations — see [`/docs/verify-route.md`](/docs/verify-route.md)) never uses `verifyServer`,
even when it's configured. It only verifies payloads locally. If a custom integration needs
remote Sentinel verification, call the exported `verifyServer()` function directly instead of
going through the plugin's `/verify` route.
